directAnswer: Pope Julius III was Giovanni Maria Ciocchi del Monte, a Roman-born canon lawyer who had presided over the opening of the Council of Trent, and he reigned from 1550 to 1555. He reconvened the council in 1551, founded the Collegium Germanicum with St. Ignatius of Loyola, and saw England briefly reconciled with Rome under Mary I, though his favoritism toward an adopted nephew caused lasting scandal.

sections.h2: Papal Legate at the Opening of Trent
paras: Giovanni Maria Ciocchi del Monte was born in Rome in 1487 to a family from Monte San Savino in Tuscany. Trained in law, he rose through the Curia, served as archbishop of Siponto, and was made a cardinal by Paul III in 1536.

In 1545 he was one of the three papal legates who presided over the first sessions of the Council of Trent, alongside Marcello Cervini and Reginald Pole. After a conclave of more than ten weeks, he was elected pope on 7 February 1550 and took the name Julius in honor of Julius II, who had first advanced his family.

Julius III reopened the Council of Trent at Trent in May 1551. In this second period the council issued important decrees on the Eucharist, penance and anointing of the sick, and some Protestant envoys from Germany briefly attended.
In April 1552 the revolt of Maurice of Saxony against Charles V threatened the city, and the council was suspended. It would not meet again for nearly ten years.

sections.h2: The Jesuits, the Collegium Germanicum, and England
paras: Julius III confirmed and expanded the Society of Jesus in 1550 with the bull Exposcit debitum. In 1552, at Ignatius of Loyola's urging, he founded the Collegium Germanicum in Rome to train priests for the German-speaking lands where Protestantism had spread.

When Mary I became queen of England in 1553, Julius sent Cardinal Pole as legate, and in November 1554 Parliament restored communion with Rome. The reconciliation lasted only until Mary's death in 1558.

sections.h2: Villa Giulia, Palestrina, and the Innocenzo Scandal
paras: Julius III spent heavily on the Villa Giulia outside Rome's walls, a refined suburban retreat designed with the help of Vignola and Ammannati that now houses the national Etruscan museum. He brought the composer Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina to Rome as choirmaster of the Cappella Giulia in 1551 and later admitted him to the papal choir.

Shortly after his election, Julius made Innocenzo Ciocchi del Monte, a teenage youth of humble origins whom his brother had adopted, a cardinal and gave him important posts. The promotion caused widespread scandal at the time, and Innocenzo's later misconduct deepened it. Julius III died on 23 March 1555.

keyFacts: Born Giovanni Maria Ciocchi del Monte in Rome in 1487
Co-presided over the opening of the Council of Trent in 1545
Reconvened the Council of Trent in May 1551
Founded the Collegium Germanicum with St. Ignatius (1552)
England reconciled with Rome under Mary I (1554)

faqs.question: What role did Julius III play at the Council of Trent?
faqs.answer: As Cardinal del Monte he was a presiding legate at its opening in 1545, and as pope he reconvened it in 1551 until war forced its suspension in 1552.

faqs.question: What was the Collegium Germanicum?
faqs.answer: A Roman seminary founded by Julius III in 1552 at the suggestion of St. Ignatius of Loyola to form priests for Germany and neighboring lands. It still operates as the Collegium Germanicum et Hungaricum.

faqs.question: Who was Innocenzo del Monte?
faqs.answer: A youth adopted by the pope's brother, whom Julius III made a cardinal at about 17. The appointment was widely criticized as an abuse of nepotism, and Innocenzo later fell into disgrace.
